concept.name: Kalman filter
concept.definition: A recursive algorithm for optimal linear estimation of the hidden state of a linear Gaussian state-space system, alternating prediction and update steps that weight new observations by their information content. Kalman (1960) derived it as the solution to the linear filtering and prediction problem.
concept.intuition: Keep a running best guess of an unobservable quantity plus your uncertainty about it; each new noisy observation nudges the guess toward the data, by more when the data are precise relative to your uncertainty.
concept.mechanics: The prediction step projects the state mean and covariance forward through the transition equation; the update step computes the Kalman gain K_t = P_{t|t-1} H' (H P_{t|t-1} H' + R)^{-1} and revises the state using the innovation y_t - H x_{t|t-1}. For linear Gaussian systems the filter is the exact minimum mean-square-error estimator; extended, unscented, and particle variants handle nonlinearity.
concept.formula: State: x_t = F x_{t-1} + w_t, w_t ~ N(0,Q); observation: y_t = H x_t + v_t, v_t ~ N(0,R); update: x_{t|t} = x_{t|t-1} + K_t (y_t - H x_{t|t-1}).
concept.failure_modes: Exact optimality holds only for linear Gaussian systems; with heavy-tailed noise the filter is merely the best linear estimator and is badly distorted by outliers. Misspecified process and observation noise covariances (Q and R) degrade or destabilize estimates.
concept.misconceptions: That the Kalman filter is a smoother: it is a causal online filter using only past and current data, while retrospective refinement requires the separate Rauch-Tung-Striebel smoother.
concept.example: In pairs trading the hedge ratio is modeled as a random-walk state observed through the spread, and the Kalman filter updates the ratio online as the relationship drifts.
